figures.finding: In England a child (to the end of compulsory school age) needs a local-authority licence to take part in a paid, broadcast or recorded performance; the 2014 Regulations set the earliest and latest times, the hours at the place of performance by age, a 12-hour overnight break, no more than six consecutive days, three hours' daily schooling by a private teacher and an approved chaperone for up to twelve children.

value.licence: child performance licence, granted by the local authority where the child lives

figures.applies: England (the Children (Performances and Activities) (England) Regulations 2014); s. 37 of the 1963 Act runs in England, Wales and Scotland, whose own regulations weren't read. The licence attaches to taking part in a performance (including taking a performer's place in rehearsal); the Act doesn't reach a child who writes or directs.

any performance recorded (by whatever means) with a view to its use in a broadcast or such a service or in a film intended for public exhibition;
Table 2 sets out the maximum number of hours a child may be at a place of performance or rehearsal, may perform or rehearse in one day and may perform or rehearse continuously.
A child must not take part in performances or rehearsals on more than six consecutive days.
a child must have an overnight break of a minimum duration of twelve hours between attendance at a place of performance or rehearsal.
total not less than three hours on each day on which the child would be required to attend school
The maximum number of children a chaperone may take care of at any one time is— (a) twelve;

figures.finding: No share of a child performer's earnings is fixed by law in England: the licensing authority may make it a condition of the licence that the earnings be dealt with in a particular way.
figures.applies: England, licensed performances. How a minor's own contract is made binding (common law) wasn't read; see blockers.

sources.said: The licensing authority may include a condition in the licence that any or all of the sums earned by the child for taking part in the performance or activity be dealt with in a particular manner by the licence holder.

figures.finding: Equity has an Under 18 membership at a subsidised rate for young performers aged 10 to 17.
figures.applies: Equity (performers). WGGB's and Directors UK's rules weren't read.

sources.said: Our subsidised rate for young performers aged between 10 and 17 (inclusive) earning less than £40,000 a year.

figures.finding: BFI NETWORK's short-film and early-feature funding is for producers, writers and directors aged 18 and above.
figures.applies: BFI NETWORK; the BFI Filmmaking Fund's own applicant rule wasn't read.

sources.said: to producers, writers and directors aged 18 and above.

figures.finding: A person must be at least sixteen to be appointed a director of a UK company; an earlier appointment is void.

sources.said: A person may not be appointed a director of a company unless he has attained the age of 16 years.

figures.finding: In Scotland a person of sixteen has full capacity to contract; one of sixteen or seventeen may later ask the court (until twenty-one) to set aside a prejudicial transaction, but not one made in the course of his trade, business or profession, nor one the court ratified beforehand on all parties' joint application; under sixteen a child can make only contracts of a kind usual for his age, on reasonable terms.

GB.SCT.16to17: a prejudicial transaction may be set aside on application before 21, except one in the course of his trade, business or profession or one ratified by the court (s 4)
GB.SCT.under16: only transactions commonly entered into by persons of his age and circumstances, on terms not unreasonable

figures.applies: Scotland, Age of Legal Capacity (Scotland) Act 1991 ss 1-4 (legislation.gov.uk, revised text).

sources.said: (a) a person under the age of 16 years shall, subject to section 2 below, have no legal capacity to enter into any transaction;  (b) a person of or over the age of 16 years shall have legal capacity to enter into any transaction.

(1) A person under the age of 16 years shall have legal capacity to enter into a transaction—  (a) of a kind commonly entered into by persons of his age and circumstances, and  (b) on terms which are not unreasonable.

(1) A person under the age of 21 years (“the applicant”) may make application to the court to set aside a transaction which he entered into while he was of or over the age of 16 years but under the age of 18 years and which is a prejudicial transaction. … (f) a transaction in the course of the applicant’s trade, business or profession;

(1) Where a person of or over the age of 16 years but under the age of 18 years proposes to enter into a transaction which, if completed, could be the subject of an application to the court under section 3 above to set aside, all parties to the proposed transaction may make a joint application to have it ratified by the court.

figures.finding: The Writers' Guild of Great Britain admits full and student members only from eighteen; its candidate membership, for those intending to qualify, states no age; Directors UK's articles admit any natural person who is the director of works, again without an age.

Directors UK.admission: any natural person who is the director of Works (articles 6.1.1)
